category: realtime pub/sub messaging over WebSocket with an HTTP publish API

free_tier.stated: Channels Sandbox: 200k messages per day and 100 concurrent connections, free
free_tier.notes: A message is each API request plus each delivery to a connected client: a publish to 50 subscribers is 51 messages. Limits are counted per account, over all the apps it owns. A warning email goes out at 80% of a limit. Past the daily message limit every trigger request answers 403 over quota; past the connection limit new connections are rejected, and on Sandbox the connection limit is enforced at once (paid plans at 120%). One trigger request reaches at most 100 channels.

per_object_cap.stated: 10KB of event data per message; a larger event answers 413
per_object_cap.notes: The page writes 10KB without saying 10,000 or 10,240 bytes, so no byte count is recorded.

retention.stated: No message history by default; an opt-in cache channel keeps the last event in memory for at most 30 minutes or until a new event arrives

egress.terms: Each delivery to a connected client counts as a message against the 200k daily quota; no byte allowance is stated

interface_detail: HTTP API at api-CLUSTER.pusher.com (for example api-mt1.pusher.com) over HTTP or HTTPS, each request signed with an HMAC SHA256 digest; clients hold WebSocket connections with an HTTP fallback transport, which the interface vocabulary has no term for. The api-mt1 host answered 400 to an unsigned request.
tooling: The pusher-js client and the Pusher server libraries, or any HTTP client that signs requests with the app secret.
chaining: A notification fan-out from a worker to a browser dashboard, sized for about 18,000 publishes a day to 10 subscribers each.

limits.value: 200k messages per day per account, deliveries included
no history; cache channels keep the last event for at most 30 minutes

limits_note: 100 concurrent connections per account, enforced at once on Sandbox, and 100 channels per trigger request. The vocabulary has no kind for a concurrency cap.
binding_note: A publish to n subscribers counts n + 1 against 200,000 a day, so a publish to 10 subscribers leaves about 18,000 publishes a day (200,000 / 11); a fan-out to more than 100 clients meets the connection cap first.

identity_cost.detail: The signup form asks for an email address and a password, or a GitHub or Google sign-in, behind an invisible reCAPTCHA; billing and card details are entered only when a plan is upgraded.

reliability_note: Over the daily message quota the HTTP API answers 403 and further publishes fail until the next day; connections over the limit are rejected at once on Sandbox.
confidence_note: Every limit is quoted from first-party pricing, documentation and support pages; the HTTP API host was probed and answered 400 to an unsigned request. No event was published, because publishing needs an app key and secret. A signed publish from a Sandbox app would move it to measured.
